newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-HART CRITICAL OF "CANCER" IN ENGLISH GAME.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-HART CRITICAL OF "CANCER" IN ENGLISH GAME.

text.p: All Black coach John Hart has denounced the political in-fighting in English rugby as "a cancer in the game" as he struggles to prepare his New Zealand Barbarians side for Saturday's match against England at Twickenham.

Hart feels his build-up was undermined when the North fielded a severely weakened team against the touring team last Sunday, following a decision by several top English clubs to withdraw their players.
The NZ Barbarians crushed the North 86-0 and, after naming a side containing 13 All Blacks for the England encounter, Hart allowed his frustration to show.

"We face a great challenge on Saturday and it was very sad this dispute affected us. It was embarrassing and I feel we were not treated with respect.We needed a decent competitive match and we didn't get one."

Mike Banks NZ Barbarians manager commented: "The game was nearly cancelled but even though we played, it was insufficient preparation. It was extremely disappointing that we were faced with such a predicament."
Jonah Lomu is back to haunt the side against whom he scored four tries in last year's World Cup semifinal, alongside two uncapped players in number eight Taine Randell and wing Joeli Vidiri.

Vidiri, a Fijian, is still qualifying for New Zealand having played eight Tests for his own country. He will not be an All Black until 1998, but Hart said: "He is a very special player and if I were coach in two years time I would be very encouraged."

Team - Christian Cullen; Joeli Vidiri, Alama Ieremia, Lee Stensness, Jonah Lomu; Andrew Mehrtens, Justin Marshall; Taine Randell, Michael Jones, Andrew Blowers, Ian Jones, Robin Brooke, Mark Allen, Sean Fitzpatrick (captain), Olo Brown.
